query: meta-agent modifies training environment during multi-turn reinforcement learning
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)** (October 2026). The closest match: a meta-agent monitors multi-turn RL training and modifies the environment, user simulator, rewards, and training configuration, hot-swapping validated changes into ongoing runs. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii). [Project page and affiliations](https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/).

2. **[Weak-for-Strong: Training Weak Meta-Agent to Harness Strong Executors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04785)** (April 2025). Related work: trains a smaller meta-agent through multi-turn RL to generate and refine workflows for stronger models. Its focus is workflow optimization rather than modifying a live training environment. **People:** Fan Nie, Haotian Ye, Weixin Liang, Pan Lu, and James Zou (Stanford University); Lan Feng and Alexandre Alahi (EPFL); Huaxiu Yao (UNC–Chapel Hill). [Paper with affiliations](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.04785).

query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19336)** (2026). Trains simulators using an LLM judge’s reward for responses indistinguishable from a real user’s. **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim (MIT); Zexue He (Stanford); Alex Pentland (MIT and Stanford); Pengyuan Li (MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab).

2. **[UserLM-R1: Modeling Human Reasoning in User Language Models with Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.09215v1)** (2026). Closely matches adaptive simulation: combines dynamic user goals, strategic reasoning, and multiple rewards to improve simulator consistency and resistance to manipulation. **People:** Feng Zhang, Shijia Li, Chunmao Zhang, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He, Jingwen Xu, and Han Liu. **Affiliations represented:** Meituan, Peking University, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Dalian University of Technology.

3. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.02208v1)** (2025). Introduces UserVille’s configurable user simulators and rewards agents for task completion, useful clarification, and alignment with user preferences. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang (Carnegie Mellon University); Xingyao Wang (OpenHands).

4. **[SalesSim: Benchmarking and Aligning Multimodal Language Models as Retail User Simulators](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.08334v1)** (2026). Introduces UserGRPO to reward persona-consistent purchasing decisions and realistic conversation in simulated shopper–agent interactions. **People:** Yada Pruksachatkun and Chien-Sheng Wu (Salesforce Research); Elaine Wan, Lyanna Chen, and Kai-Wei Chang (UCLA).

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04872)** (2026). The closest match: adapts agent coordination and memory **within runs**, then distills trajectories into model weights **across runs**. **People:** Wenxiao Zhao, Dong Liu, Kaiyi Xu, Lei Bai, and colleagues. **Affiliations:** Shanghai AI Laboratory, UCLA, and Tongji University.

2. **[PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26530)** (2026). Combines live supervisor intervention during execution with persistent skills and memory for subsequent runs; model weights stay frozen. **People:** Yang Xiao, Yusong Sun, Haoyi Wu, Chengyue Jiang, and colleagues. **Team affiliation:** AllSpark Team, as credited in the paper.

3. **[RL²: Fast Reinforcement Learning via Slow Reinforcement Learning](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=HkLXCE9lx)** (2016). Foundational work connecting rapid adaptation through recurrent state with slower training of the learning algorithm across tasks. **People and affiliations:** Yan Duan, John Schulman, Xi Chen, and Pieter Abbeel—UC Berkeley and OpenAI; Peter L. Bartlett—UC Berkeley; Ilya Sutskever—OpenAI. Affiliations are those listed in the paper.

2. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24426)** — May 2026. 3. **[Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18292)** — April 2026. 4. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19682)** — December 2025. query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** — The closest match: eight interactive tasks, with simulated speakers, offline datasets, and online environments for training and evaluating RL algorithms. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, and Yuexiang Zhai (UC Berkeley); Kelvin Xu (Google DeepMind); Sergey Levine (UC Berkeley and Google DeepMind).

2. **[UserBench: An Interactive Gym Environment for User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22034v1)** — Simulated users reveal preferences gradually, testing whether agents clarify vague goals and satisfy user intent across multiple turns. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research and UIUC), Heng Ji (UIUC), and Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Zhiwei Liu, Jianguo Zhang, Haolin Chen, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

3. **[τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.07982v1)** — A benchmark where both agents and simulated users operate tools, testing communication and coordination in shared environments. **People:** Victor Barres, Soham Ray, and Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra); Honghua Dong (Sierra, University of Toronto, and Vector Institute); Xujie Si (University of Toronto and Vector Institute).

4. **[MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18669v1)** — A related training framework that integrates simulated users into RL and evaluates on τ-bench, τ²-Bench, BFCL, and ACEBench. **People:** Weikang Zhao (Meituan and Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences); Xili Wang (Meituan and Peking University); Chengdi Ma (Peking University); Lingbin Kong, Zhaohua Yang, Mingxiang Tuo, Xiaowei Shi, Yitao Zhai, and Xunliang Cai (Meituan).

query: methods improving user-centric agents with simulated users
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)** (2026). Uses a meta-agent to improve user simulators, environments, rewards, and RL settings as training progresses. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), and Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19736)** (2025). Trains agents through simulated-user interactions across eight task environments; studies reward shaping, trajectory scoring, and simulator choice. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research and UIUC), Heng Ji (UIUC), and Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

3. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02208)** (2025). Introduces **UserVille**, with preference-aware simulated users, and **PPP**, which jointly rewards task completion, useful clarification, and personalization. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang (Carnegie Mellon University), with Xingyao Wang (OpenHands); the team also lists OpenHands affiliation.

4. **[MIMESIS: Learning User Simulators as Training Environments for Interactive Agents](https://viethoang1512.github.io/mimesis/)** (2026). Trains realistic user simulators from human conversations, then uses their simulated reactions and private reasoning to coach agents during training. **People:** Hoang Phan (Meta and NYU), Changdae Oh (Meta and University of Wisconsin–Madison), and Dat Huynh, Andrey Zhmoginov, Qi Zeng, Wancen Mu, Yue Cao, Shengjie Bi, Yun He, and Deren Lei; the project is from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
